title: release-train-weekly-prep-notes-zara-ali-2026-06-17
content:
Release train weekly prep notes (quick scratchpad) - 2026-06-17
Owner: Zara Ali
Attendees (for reference): Samir P., Maya S., Noah K., infra on-call (TBD)
Context: final run-up for feature rollout (v2.3) scheduled week of 2026-06-22. This doc is my personal prep for the weekly go/no-go sync and to capture outstanding actions.

Goals for sync:
- Quick health check across serving/runtime, infra, rollout config, and client SDKs
- Confirm go/no-go decision criteria status and owners for any outstanding items
- Align on cutover window and rollback triggers

Quick decision matrix (my draft):
- Must-have (all must be green to go):
  - Performance regression tests <= 5% p50/p95 delta (owner: Samir) — status: in_progress (running final sweep today)
  - Error budget for release route < 0.5% (owner: Maya) — status: blocked (investigating spike from canary)
  - Migration script applied to staging and validated (owner: Noah) — status: done
  - E2E smoke tests passed for core flows (owner: QE) — status: in_progress (queue: 3 flaky tests)
- Nice-to-have (prefer green but not blocker):
  - Observability dashboards updated with new routes (owner: Observability) — status: partial
  - Release notes and customer comms drafted (owner: Product PM) — status: draft

Checklist (for meeting review)
1) Canary results: duration, error rate, latency breakdown, KV cache hit rate — owner Samir — note: spike at 11:40am on canary-2, root cause hypothesis: batching misconfig when sequence length > 1024
2) Autoscaling and capacity reservation verified for peak load — owner: Infra (Noah supports) — note: reserved pool applied, but autoscaler threshold needs tuning
3) DB/migration lock window confirmed and ops runbook ready — owner: Noah — note: migration applied to staging; ops runbook draft attached
4) Rollout policy config in Console (canary %, step cadence, automatic rollback thresholds) — owner: Maya — note: current plan = 5% -> 25% -> 60% -> 100% with 30m watch per step
5) Client SDK compatibility check (web + mobile) — owner: SDK team — note: web ok, iOS flagged one minor serialization change
6) Security & compliance signoff (KMS, audit logs) — owner: Security — note: pending quick review of new KMS key usage pattern
7) Post-release metrics to monitor and alert thresholds (cost, latency, error, cache efficiency) — owner: Observability — note: draft alerts exist, need tuning for p95 threshold

Open/blocking items (to escalate in sync)
- Error spike on canary-2 (Maya/Samir): stack traces show transient gRPC timeouts. Need infra to validate network flapping or kernel-level drops.
- Two flaky E2E tests (QE): blocking final signoff. Quick triage scheduled 9:30am — invite QE, Samir.
- iOS SDK serialization discrepancy: risk of minor client errors for small fraction of users. Decide whether to include iOS fix in this train or patch post-release. (Owner: SDK lead)

Proposed meeting agenda (15–20m):
- 0–3m: quick status (owners call out green/yellow/red)
- 3–8m: review canary metrics + immediate blockers
- 8–12m: confirm must-haves and outstanding actions, assign owners
- 12–16m: cutover window + rollback triggers confirmation
- 16–20m: final go/no-go vote and next steps

Action items I want to own/check before meeting:
- Follow up with Infra on network health logs for canary-2 (Zara) — due: today EOD
- Get QE triage notes and link failing test runs in Confluence (Zara) — due: 9:15am 2026-06-17
- Confirm ops on-call for rollback (Zara -> Ops) — due: before sync

Other notes / quick links:
- Staging canary dashboard: link (pinned in Confluence)
- Rollout config JSON: s3://redwood-artifacts/release/2026-06-17/rollout-config.json
- Manual rollback procedure: Confluence -> Runbooks -> Release rollback

Questions to ask in sync:
- Do we accept a 1–2% transient error blip during first hour if automatic rollback triggers are in place? (my inclination: no, prefer to fix pre-rollout)
- Is the iOS serialization bug trivial enough for hotfix post-release or should we delay? Need SDK lead opinion

Scratch/TODO (personal):
- If error spike root cause is batching config, keep ready a quick flag in config to force single-request path for affected routes (owner: Samir)
- Prepare short customer-facing note template in case we need to alert mid-rollout (owner: Product)

Bottom line (my read): a couple of last-mile infra & QE items — currently yellow. If canary spike root cause is transient infra and QE fixes tests quickly, we can still hit go. Otherwise be prepared to postpone 24–48h.

-- Zara
